text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- CENTRAL BANK SURPRISES THE MARKET AND CUTS TBC TO 1.82 PCT

The Central Bank reduced on Monday its Basic Interest Rate (TBC) to 1.82 percent for October from 1.88 percent in September. The new TBC was below market expectations, which means that a drop in interbank interest rates is likely to happen.
The Central Bank also set the first Rate of Assistance of the Central Bank (TBAN) at 1.93 percent.
-- CND DECIDES TODAY ON PORTS SELLOFF

The National Privatization Council (CND) meets today in Brasilia to prepare the privatization of Brazilian ports. The CND members will examine the proposal to transfer to private investors four ports by the end of the year: Itajai, Laguna, Cabedelo and Porto Velho. A total of 27 ports will be privatized.
-- BANKS RECOMMEND BRAHMA SHARES
Shares of Brazilian brewery Brahma received eight buy recommendations in 13 bank reports distributed to foreign investors.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- CEF REVIEWS HOUSING CONTRACTS
Federal bank Caixa Economica Federal (CEF) will announce a package of measures to help mortgage holders to refinance their debts.
-- FARMERS OFFER LANDS TO LANDLESS

A group of farmers from Teodoro Sampaio, in Sao Paulo state, is willing to offer lands to landless people. In exchange, they want the Incra and the Sao Paulo state government to include these properties in the agrarian reform at Pontal do Paranapanema.
O GLOBO
-- GOV'T TO ASK 450,000 PUBLIC SERVANTS TO PAY DEBTS
The Administration Ministry decided to request 450,000 federal public workers to pay off a debt totalling 149.5 million reais. The debt refers to social security contributions.
-- BRAZIL INVESTIGATES U.S. DUMPING
The Ministry of Industry and Commerce started anti-dumping probes against imports of inseticides from Chile, a rubber product from the U.S. and glasswort from Bulgaria, Poland, Romania and Spain.
-- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- Fatima Cristina, Sao Paulo newsroom, 55-11-2324411
